title: Motion on Singapore's economic future, amended and agreed to
what_it_is: A Motion moved by Mr Kenneth Tiong and seconded by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, proposing principles for a more equal and inclusive economy and an economic engine driven by local companies, domestic demand and Singaporeans venturing abroad, which was debated and amended.
why_it_matters: The amended Motion records the House's belief in a more equal and inclusive economy and an economy powered by dynamic local companies, global enterprises, healthy domestic and external demand, and Singaporeans and Singaporean capital venturing abroad. The transcript does not state any direct change to law or schemes from the Motion itself. The record does not set out the practical impact.

key_points.point: He proposed a special zone around NTU where state land is charged at cost recovery rather than market scarcity value.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: What we should create a special zone surrounding Nanyang Technological University (NTU), where the state land is charged as cost recovery rather than market scarcity value

key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)

what_happens_next: The amended Motion was agreed to; the WP recorded its dissent. The transcript does not state any further step.
not_said: Whether mandatory retrenchment benefits will be legislated, and what impact that would have on employers, SMEs and hiring.

How many Enterprise Singapore-supported SMEs that applied for internationalisation programmes succeeded and remained in foreign markets after five years, and what the internal rate of return for those grants is.
Whether the Government will adopt the proposed NTU special zone, the new land use category for restricted tenure, non-tradable, mixed housing and enterprise land, or the proposed zone authority.
Whether the Government will cap annual rent increases for SMEs or revisit dependency ratio ceilings for sectors such as F&B.
What specific macroeconomic targets beyond top-line growth the Government will commit to, and whether a consolidated report card for the four economic blueprints will be published.
Whether the Government will set a target for Singapore-headquartered companies with more than $1 billion in revenue.
How the proposed shared use of research labs and equipment would be managed.
Whether the Government will expand funding lines for early-stage high-failure, high-impact deep tech ventures as proposed.
What the practical impact of the amended Motion will be for ordinary Singaporeans.
